groups.h: check a file, link or hash

items.w: Scan a file hash, URL, domain or IP against ~70 AV engines and see what others found.
items.c: Uploads are PUBLIC to paying customers. Search by hash first; never upload private or work files.

items.w: Free sandbox report: what a sample did when run (processes, network, dropped files).
items.c: Same rule: submissions can be shared.

items.w: Interactive malware sandbox: watch a sample run live in a VM.
items.c: Free tier reports are public.

items.w: Safely load a suspicious link and see screenshot, redirects, requests and hosting.
items.c: Public scans are listed; mark private if the URL contains tokens.

items.w: Look up and download known malware samples by hash (for lab use only).
items.c: Handle only inside an isolated VM.

items.w: Decode base64, hex, XOR, URL encoding and more by chaining operations. Runs in your browser.
Paste an unsalted hash (MD5, SHA-1, NTLM...) and it looks it up in a huge table of known passwords. Shows why weak and unsalted hashes are dangerous.
items.c: Only hashes from your own labs or CTFs. Never paste a real account's hash: you'd be sending it to a stranger.

items.w: The GPU password-auditing tool, like John the Ripper. Used on your own lab to test how fast weak passwords fall.
items.c: Authorized targets only.

items.w: Paste a hash to see which type it is (MD5, bcrypt, NTLM...) before choosing a tool.
items.c: Lab hashes only.

items.n: Have I Been Pwned: Pwned Passwords
items.w: Check if a password is in known breaches. Uses k-anonymity, so the full password never leaves your browser.
items.c: Still prefer the range API or a password manager's built-in check.

items.w: Is my email in a known breach? Also check passwords through the k-anonymity range search.
items.c: Only enter your own addresses.

items.w: Check a domain's MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, blacklists and header analysis.
Paste an email's headers to see the path and delays. Good for phishing triage.
items.c: Headers can contain addresses: redact before sharing.

items.w: Reputation lookup for an email address (age, spam and breach signals).
See old versions of a page, recover deleted content, or save a snapshot as evidence.
Snapshot a page you want to preserve without visiting it again.
Search engine for internet-connected devices. Great for checking YOUR OWN exposure.
items.c: Look, don't touch anything that isn't yours.

items.w: Certificate transparency search: find subdomains and certificates for a domain.
Is this IP reported for attacks? Check suspicious IPs from your logs.
Domain age and registrar. A days-old domain in an email is a red flag.
Pick apps (Chrome, 7-Zip, VLC...) and get ONE installer that silently installs them with no toolbars. Handy for fresh Windows builds.
items.c: Only from ninite.com.

groups.h: bug bounty and web hacking: free training

items.w: Free, self-paced web security course with a hands-on lab for every topic (SQL injection, XSS, access control, SSRF and more). The best free place to start.
items.c: Labs are made to be attacked. Never use these techniques on real sites you do not have written permission to test.

items.w: HackerOne's free video classes plus a CTF where flags teach real web bugs. Written for people who want to start bounty hunting.
items.c: The CTF is in a controlled environment; real programs have rules, see below.

items.w: Guided browser-based rooms with a target machine provided. The web and bug bounty related paths are a gentle start. I use this one.
items.c: Some rooms and paths need a paid subscription; the free tier is enough to start.

items.w: A deliberately insecure web shop to attack on your own machine, with a score board and hints.
items.c: Run it locally or in a container, not exposed to the internet.

items.w: Guided lessons on common web flaws in a vulnerable Java app.
items.c: Same rule: local only.

items.w: The list of most common web risks. Read it before the labs so the names mean something.
Free videos and slides on bug bounty methods from a bounty platform.
Public bounty programs and their scope and rules, so you can see what a real policy says.
items.c: Read the scope and safe-harbor policy of any program before you test anything. Out-of-scope testing can be illegal.

items.w: Another list of public programs and disclosure policies.
items.c: Same warning: stay in scope, no data access beyond proof, report quickly.

items.w: Exercises and badges on web bugs; the free section has a good number of exercises.
items.c: Most of the library is paid.
